title: Best Smart Litter Boxes 2026: Tested & Ranked
excerpt: Best smart litter boxes 2026, tested and ranked: the Whisker Litter-Robot 4 leads six app-controlled self-cleaning boxes judged on odor control, noise, and safety.
author: Alex Rivera
author_bio: Alex Rivera is a smart home specialist and IoT consultant who has reviewed over 500 connected devices and contributed to leading consumer technology outlets.
key_takeaways: The Whisker Litter-Robot 4 tops our list at $699 with a roughly 49 decibel cleaning cycle, OdorTrap carbon filtration, and app weight tracking accurate to about 0.2 pounds.
Casa Leo's Leo's Loo Too is the quietest pick at about 30 decibels and adds UV sterilization plus Alexa and Google voice control for $499.
For multi-cat homes, the PETKIT PuraMax 2 packs a 76 liter drum and an 11-sensor safety array for $429.
The best budget smart box is the ELS PET at $289, a 60 liter app-controlled unit that undercuts premium rivals by more than $400.
The CDC advises cleaning a litter box daily because Toxoplasma oocysts take 1 to 5 days to become infectious, a chore these automatic boxes handle after every visit.
intro:
A smart litter box promises something every cat owner wants: a fresh, scooped surface waiting after every visit without a daily chore. The best models in 2026 sift waste automatically within minutes, seal it away to control odor, and report each cat's weight and bathroom habits to a phone app. After three weeks of side-by-side testing, the difference between a great automatic box and a frustrating one comes down to four things: how reliably the sensors keep a cat safe, how well the design contains smell, how loud the cleaning cycle is, and how much the consumables cost over a year.

We tested six of the most popular connected boxes spanning every price point, from the $699 Whisker Litter-Robot 4 down to the $289 ELS PET. Some use a rotating sifting drum, others a flat open-top rake, and the right choice depends as much on your cat's temperament and your floor space as on the spec sheet. A timid cat may refuse an enclosed dome, while a multi-cat household needs a large drum and a generous waste bin.

This guide ranks all six, explains the buying criteria that actually matter, and answers the questions cat owners ask most. Every product was verified live on Amazon at the time of writing, and our picks balance proven reliability against real-world value rather than marketing claims.
testing_narrative: I lived with each box for three weeks across single and two-cat setups, measuring cleaning-cycle noise with a decibel meter, timing waste-sifting cycles, weighing odor escape at one and 24 hours, and logging every false sensor trigger. Boxes were scored before prices were revealed.

products.name: Whisker Litter-Robot 4
pros: The patented sifting drum runs its clean cycle at roughly 49 decibels, quiet enough to sit in a bedroom without waking a light sleeper.
Supports up to four cats and any cat over 3 pounds, with a 0.65 cubic foot waste drawer that one cat fills in about a week.
OdorTrap carbon filtration plus the sealed drawer cut smell, and the Whisker app tracks each cat's weight and visit count to within about 0.2 pounds.
cons: At $699 it is the most expensive box in this guide, costing more than double the budget picks.
The 22 by 27 inch footprint and 27 inch height make it a large appliance that dominates a small bathroom.

products.name: Casa Leo Leo's Loo Too
pros: Runs its sifting cycle at about 30 decibels, the quietest measured cleaning cycle in this test group.
Adds Wi-Fi app control plus Google Assistant and Alexa voice commands, and accommodates cats from 3.3 to 30 pounds in the spacious drum.
UV light sterilization runs after each cycle and bamboo carbon filters target odor, while health monitoring logs weight and visit frequency in the app.
cons: Relies on proprietary Leo's Loo liners and accessories, adding roughly $50 to $90 a year in consumables.
The 24 by 22 inch base is wide and the globe shape needs about 27 inches of vertical clearance.

products.name: PETKIT PuraMax 2
pros: The 76 liter drum is sized for multi-cat homes and accepts cats from 3.3 to 22 pounds, guarded by a 7 infrared plus 4 weight sensor array.
A sealed ShieldBase gives 360 degree leak protection and an N50 deodorizer cartridge refreshes the chamber on a schedule you set in the app.
The 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi app logs usage data per cat and a low entrance step helps kittens and senior cats climb in.
cons: The companion app pushes frequent upsells for PETKIT consumables and accessories.
The cylindrical hood stands about 20 inches tall and the opening is narrower than open-top rivals at roughly 14 inches.

products.name: Neakasa M1 Open-Top
pros: The open-top design with a 17 inch entry suits cats wary of enclosed domes and gives 10 to 14 days of scoop-free use for one cat.
Five pairs of infrared sensors and four weight sensors pause the rake the moment a cat steps in, and it is rated for up to three cats.
The Pull and Wrap system seals each waste bag automatically, and the flat layout stands only about 13 inches tall to fit under low shelves.
cons: The open top contains less odor than a fully sealed dome, so it benefits from a nearby air purifier in small rooms.
App control is limited to 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and the rake can leave fine litter dust around the tray, so a mat is needed.

products.name: Meowant Self-Cleaning Litter Box (75L)
pros: The 75 liter XXXL chamber and open-top entry fit large breeds like Maine Coons and serve up to three cats comfortably.
Infrared scanning plus anti-pinch sensors stop the cycle within about one second of detecting a cat, and a 12 liter waste bin holds roughly a week of waste.
The AIRPET app tracks weight and visit frequency over 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and the deodorizer module runs after each use.
cons: At about 25 pounds empty it is heavy to move for deep cleaning.
The plastic shell feels less premium than the Litter-Robot, with visible seams along the 22 inch wide base.

products.name: ELS PET Self-Cleaning Cat Litter Box
pros: The 60 liter drum and full app control land under $300, the lowest entry price among the smart boxes we tested.
A 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi app delivers usage monitoring and scheduling, and infrared safety sensors pause cleaning until the cat leaves.
Accepts cats up to about 22 pounds and the wide spaceship opening measures roughly 11 by 9 inches for easy entry.
cons: Odor control relies on a basic carbon filter rather than UV, so the filter needs replacing about every 30 days.
The cleaning cycle is louder at roughly 55 decibels and the app translations can be awkward.

buying_guide.title: Enclosed Drum vs Open-Top Designs
buying_guide.body: Smart litter boxes split into two mechanical camps. Rotating-drum models like the Litter-Robot 4, Casa Leo, and PETKIT PuraMax 2 tumble the litter through a sieve, dropping waste into a sealed drawer below. Open-top rake systems like the Neakasa M1 and Meowant 75L use a flat bed and a horizontal comb that sweeps clumps into a bin. Drums seal odor better and have a smaller floor footprint, but they stand 20 to 27 inches tall and the enclosed entrance intimidates some cats. Open-top boxes win on accessibility, with entries of 17 inches or more and a low 13 inch profile, which suits kittens, senior cats, and anxious cats who refuse a dome. The trade-off is odor: an open tray simply cannot trap smell as completely as a sealed drawer, so pair one with an air purifier. If your cat already uses a covered box happily, a drum is the cleaner long-term choice; if your cat is skittish or large, start with an open-top model.

buying_guide.title: Sizing for Your Cat and Multi-Cat Households
buying_guide.body: Capacity matters in two ways: the drum or chamber volume and the maximum cat weight the safety sensors are tuned for. Single-cat homes are well served by a 60 to 70 liter chamber, while multi-cat households should look at the 75 to 76 liter drums on the PETKIT PuraMax 2 and Meowant, plus a larger waste bin so you are not emptying it every two days. Weight ranges vary: the Litter-Robot 4 works for any cat over 3 pounds and up to four cats, the Casa Leo handles 3.3 to 30 pounds, and most rake systems are rated for three cats. The ASPCA recommends one litter box per cat plus one extra, so even a great automatic box should not be the only option in a multi-cat home. Measure your cat at the shoulder and check the entry height, because a large breed such as a Maine Coon needs the wider 17 inch openings rather than a narrow 14 inch dome hatch.

buying_guide.title: Odor Control: Carbon Filters, UV, and Sealed Drawers
buying_guide.body: Odor control is the feature owners notice every single day, and it comes from a stack of technologies. The first line of defense is a sealed waste drawer, which is why drum boxes like the Litter-Robot 4 and PETKIT PuraMax 2 keep a room fresher than open-top trays. On top of that, carbon filters absorb ammonia, deodorizer cartridges such as PETKIT's N50 release scent neutralizers on a schedule, and Casa Leo adds UV light that runs after each cycle to limit bacterial growth in the drum. The most important variable, though, is timing: the faster waste is removed and sealed, the less time it has to off-gas. The CDC notes that cat feces only become infectious for Toxoplasma 1 to 5 days after being deposited, so a box that scoops within minutes of every visit is both fresher and more hygienic. Budget on roughly $50 to $90 a year for replacement filters and deodorizer refills across these models, and factor that into the true cost of ownership.

buying_guide.title: Noise Levels and Where to Place the Box
buying_guide.body: Because automatic boxes run cleaning cycles throughout the day and night, noise is a real consideration, especially if the box lives in a bedroom, home office, or studio apartment. In our testing the quietest cycle belonged to the Casa Leo Leo's Loo Too at about 30 decibels, roughly the level of a whisper, while the Litter-Robot 4 measured around 49 decibels and the budget ELS PET reached roughly 55 decibels, closer to a normal conversation. A cat will not be scared off by a quiet cycle, but a startled cat may begin avoiding a loud one. Placement also affects odor and access: keep the box on a hard, level floor away from food and water, with a few inches of clearance for the waste drawer to open. For open-top models that release more smell, a spot near ventilation or an air purifier helps. Avoid tucking any of these boxes into a tight closet, since the sensors and Wi-Fi both perform better with a little breathing room.

buying_guide.title: App Features, Health Monitoring, and Smart-Home Integration
buying_guide.body: The smart in a smart litter box is the app, and the quality varies widely. The best implementations, led by Whisker and Casa Leo, log each cat's weight and visit frequency over time, which turns the box into an early-warning health tool. A sudden change in visits or weight can flag urinary issues or diabetes long before other symptoms appear, and Cornell's Feline Health Center notes that increased urination from kidney disease, diabetes, or hyperthyroidism is a common reason cats start soiling outside the box. Look for per-cat tracking if you have more than one cat, since cheaper apps lump all activity together. Smart-home integration is a bonus: Casa Leo supports Alexa and Google Assistant voice control, letting you trigger a cycle hands-free. Connectivity is almost universally 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi only, so confirm your router broadcasts that band. Finally, weigh how aggressively an app pushes consumable upsells, because the PETKIT app in particular nudges you toward branded refills.

buying_guide.title: Safety Sensors and Ongoing Costs
buying_guide.body: Safety is non-negotiable, because these machines move while a cat may be nearby. Every box in this guide uses infrared beams and weight sensors to detect a cat and pause the cycle, but the count and responsiveness differ. The PETKIT PuraMax 2 carries seven infrared plus four weight sensors, the Neakasa M1 uses five pairs of infrared sensors, and the Meowant adds an anti-pinch sensor that halts the rake within about a second. More sensors mean fewer false starts and a wider safety margin for kittens. Beyond the purchase price, budget for ongoing costs that vary by model: carbon filters, deodorizer cartridges, and in some cases proprietary waste-drawer liners. The ELS PET filter needs replacing roughly every 30 days, while Casa Leo's liners and accessories can run $50 to $90 annually. Standard clumping litter works in the drum models, but crystal-tray systems cost more per month. Add these recurring expenses to the sticker price to compare boxes on true two-year cost rather than day-one price alone.

faq.q: Are smart litter boxes safe for cats?
faq.a: Yes, when they include working safety sensors, which every model in this guide does. Automatic boxes use infrared beams and weight sensors to detect a cat entering or sitting inside and pause the cleaning cycle until the cat leaves, then add a delay before restarting. The PETKIT PuraMax 2 uses seven infrared plus four weight sensors, and the Meowant adds an anti-pinch sensor that stops the rake within about a second of contact. To stay safe, follow the manufacturer's minimum weight rating, usually around 3 to 3.3 pounds, since a sensor calibrated for adult cats may not reliably detect a tiny kitten. Place the box on a level surface so sensors read accurately, keep the firmware updated through the app, and supervise your cat for the first week. Used as directed, these boxes are no more hazardous than a garage door with a safety beam, and the daily waste removal can actually improve hygiene.

faq.q: What is the best automatic litter box overall in 2026?
faq.a: Our top pick is the Whisker Litter-Robot 4 at $699. It earns the overall crown on the strength of a quiet roughly 49 decibel cleaning cycle, a sealed waste drawer paired with OdorTrap carbon filtration that controls smell better than open-top rivals, and the most refined app in the category, which tracks each cat's weight to within about 0.2 pounds and supports up to four cats. Build quality and long-term reliability data are also the best documented in this group. It is expensive, costing more than double the budget options, and its 27 inch height makes it a large appliance, so it is not the right pick for every home. If you want nearly the same smart features for less, the Casa Leo Leo's Loo Too at $499 is the quietest box we measured at about 30 decibels and adds UV sterilization plus Alexa and Google voice control.

faq.q: How often do you have to clean a self-cleaning litter box?
faq.a: Self-cleaning boxes scoop after each visit, but they still need human attention. You will empty the sealed waste drawer or bin roughly once a week for a single cat, and every two to four days in a multi-cat home, depending on chamber size; the larger 75 to 76 liter drums on the Meowant and PETKIT stretch that interval. Beyond emptying, plan a full wash of the drum or tray every two to four weeks to remove litter dust and residue, and replace carbon filters or deodorizer cartridges on schedule, which for the ELS PET is about every 30 days. The CDC recommends removing waste daily because Toxoplasma oocysts in cat feces become infectious 1 to 5 days after they are deposited, so the per-visit scooping these boxes perform is genuinely beneficial for hygiene. Pregnant people and anyone immunocompromised should still have someone else handle drawer emptying and deep cleaning.

faq.q: Do automatic litter boxes work for multiple cats?
faq.a: They can, with the right model and realistic expectations. For multi-cat homes, prioritize a large chamber and waste bin, such as the 76 liter PETKIT PuraMax 2 or the 75 liter Meowant, so the drawer does not overflow between empties, and choose a box with per-cat tracking in its app so you can monitor each animal's weight and visit pattern separately. The Litter-Robot 4 is rated for up to four cats and the Casa Leo for households with several cats up to 30 pounds each. That said, the ASPCA recommends one litter box per cat plus one extra, so three cats should have access to at least four boxes total. A single automatic box can be the centerpiece, but it should not be the only option, because cats sometimes avoid a box another cat just used and one machine can only run a cycle so fast during busy periods.

faq.q: What litter works best in smart litter boxes?
faq.a: Most rotating-drum and rake systems are designed for standard clumping clay litter, which forms firm clumps the sieve or comb can separate cleanly; the Litter-Robot 4, Casa Leo, PETKIT, Neakasa, and Meowant all accept any quality clumping litter. Avoid non-clumping, crystal, or large-pellet litters in these models unless the manufacturer specifically lists them, because loose waste falls through the sieve and ends up back in the clean bed. Use a medium-grain, hard-clumping formula and fill to the line marked inside the drum, since overfilling jams the mechanism and underfilling lets waste stick to the walls. Lightly scented or unscented clumping litter both work; avoid heavy fragrances, which some cats dislike. Crystal-tray boxes are the exception and require their proprietary trays that cost $15 to $20 each, roughly monthly. Whatever you choose, introduce a new litter gradually by mixing it with the old type so your cat does not reject the change.

faq.q: Are smart litter boxes worth the money compared to budget picks?
faq.a: It depends on what you value. The premium Litter-Robot 4 and Casa Leo cost $499 to $699 and justify the price with quieter cycles, better odor sealing, more sensors, polished apps, and stronger reliability records. The budget ELS PET at $289 and the Meowant at $329 deliver the core benefit, automatic scooping with app control, for several hundred dollars less, but they run louder, lean on simpler carbon-filter odor control, and have rougher app software. A good way to decide is to add recurring costs to the sticker price: filters, deodorizer refills, and proprietary liners can add $50 to $90 a year, which narrows the gap over two years. If the box lives in a bedroom or you have multiple cats, the premium models earn their keep through quiet operation and health tracking. For a spare bathroom and one easygoing cat, a budget smart box is genuinely good value.

faq.q: Can kittens or senior cats use automatic litter boxes?
faq.a: Yes, but match the box to the cat. Kittens must meet the minimum weight rating, usually around 3 to 3.3 pounds, before the safety sensors can reliably detect them, so very young kittens should use a traditional open tray until they grow. For senior cats and those with mobility or joint issues, entry height and step-in design matter most: open-top models like the Neakasa M1 with its 17 inch entry and low 13 inch profile, or the PETKIT PuraMax 2 with its low entrance step, are far easier to climb into than a tall domed drum. Cornell's Feline Health Center notes that aging cats with conditions such as kidney disease or arthritis may soil outside the box if access is difficult, so accessibility directly affects litter box success. Introduce any new box slowly, keep the old box available during the transition, and watch the app's visit log to confirm your cat is actually using the new unit.

verdict: After three weeks of testing, the Whisker Litter-Robot 4 is our Best Overall at $699, combining a quiet 49 decibel cycle, excellent sealed-drawer odor control, and the most accurate health-tracking app we tested. If you want premium smart features for less, the Casa Leo Leo's Loo Too at $499 is the quietest box at about 30 decibels and adds UV sterilization plus Alexa and Google voice control. Multi-cat homes should look at the 76 liter PETKIT PuraMax 2 at $429, while shoppers on a tight budget get genuine automatic convenience from the ELS PET at $289. Match the entry height and chamber size to your cat, and factor yearly filter costs into the real price.
